skip_reason: Not a sales call. This is a post-move service-recovery and refund negotiation with an existing customer (Matthew Bowen) whose move went badly. Frank is acting as branch/regional management reconstructing the job, apologizing across touchpoints, and negotiating a goodwill refund (landed at $3,800 back on a Visa ending 1209), with damages handed off to the customer experience team. No quote, no pricing pitch, no booking attempt — the sales scorecard does not apply.
top_strength: Frank did the homework before dialing — he reviewed the virtual walkthrough recording, the confirmation email, and the billing trail, then named Einstein's own failures out loud (missed trip fee and overnight fee on the confirmation, no updated confirmation after the packing change, a missing day-one invoice) instead of making the customer prove them. He also protected the customer's tip explicitly, confirming the refund would not dip into the movers' gratuity.
coaching_note: Not gradeable on the sales rubric, but worth noting for the ops loop: Frank identified a concrete, repeatable sales-process defect on this account — the walkthrough rep let the packing/boxes scope flip mid-call (customer mentioned a U-Haul) without re-probing, and the confirmation email then went out missing the trip fee and overnight fee, and was never reissued after the move shifted to three days. That is exactly the estimate-accuracy failure pattern; make sure the coaching he promised that rep actually gets logged, and that 'reissue the confirmation whenever scope changes' becomes a rule rather than a one-off fix.
phone_presence_notes: Frank absorbed heavy frustration without defensiveness, built real rapport over a shared music interest, and the customer ended the call saying he respects someone who 'stands and takes it' and would consider Einstein for a move next year.
